title: Chris Rock’s Return To Academy Event Reignites Will Smith Slap Jokes As Fans Tell Him To ‘Wear A Helmet’

 Alex Oriaifo Mon, 16 November 2026 at 11:45 pm UTC 5 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Chris Rock’s Return To Academy Event Reignites Will Smith Slap Jokes As Fans Tell Him To ‘Wear A Helmet’ Chris Rock has found himself at the center of another round of Will Smith jokes after returning to an Academy event. The comedian attended the 17th Governors Awards in Los Angeles on Sunday, November 15, more than four years after his infamous encounter with Smith at the Oscars.
 While Rock looked sharp in his formal attire, his appearance quickly brought back memories of the viral 2022 incident. Fans flooded the Academy's Instagram post with jokes about the slap, with some even offering cheeky advice on how to avoid another confrontation.
 The reactions come just months after Rock shared his thoughts on returning to the Oscars and how he feels about the incident today.
 Chris Rock Returns To Academy Event Four Years After Will Smith Slap
 C Flanigan/imageSPACE / MEGA
 Rock attended the 17th Governors Awards at the Ray Dolby Ballroom in Ovation Hollywood on Sunday. The 61-year-old comedian looked sharp in a dark gray suit, black tie, and matching shoes as he posed for photographs at the star-studded gathering.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Some of Hollywood's biggest names gathered at the event to celebrate achievements in filmmaking. Glenn Close, Ridley Scott, and Floyd Norman received honorary Oscars, while producers Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler were presented with the Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award.
 Rock's latest film, " Misty Green ," has been generating Oscar buzz, which makes his attendance even more notable. The comedian wrote and directed the A24 drama, which stars Rosalind Eleazar, Adam Driver , and Daniel Kaluuya.
 The Governors Awards are separate from the annual Oscars ceremony, but regardless, Rock's presence at an Academy-organized event was enough to revive memories of the night Will Smith slapped him on live TV.
 Fans Tell Chris Rock To 'Wear A Helmet' As Will Smith Jokes Take Over Academy Post
 View this post on Instagram 
 A post shared by The Academy (@theacademy) 
 The Academy celebrated Rock's appearance by sharing a new portrait of him on Instagram. However, many of the comments focused less on the actor's outfit and more on his famous altercation with Smith.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Will Smith has the chance to do the funniest thing possible," one fan joked, hinting at a repeat of the infamous incident.
 Another user ventured some advice, writing, "Wear a helmet."
 Other netizens joined in, with someone else commenting, "I hope the awards don't slap too hard tonight." Yet another fan poked fun at Rock's leaning pose in the picture, suggesting he still looked affected by the slap: "He's still leaning to the side from the slap."
 Amidst the barrage of jokes, one commenter was uninterested in revisiting the incident, writing, "Nah bro give the guy a break," in Rock's defense.
 Chris Rock revealed his one condition for returning to the Oscars.
 Jada Pinkett Smith claimed the comedian asked her out amid Will Smith divorce rumors.
 Chris Rock said he was "still hot" after the infamous Oscars slap .
 The comedian reportedly "stormed out" at a billionaire's party.
 Chris Rock reveals why Adam Driver calls him "every 6 to 8 months." 
 Chris Rock's Infamous 'G.I. Jane' Joke Resurfaces Among Fans
 MEGA
 Several commenters used the opportunity to bring up the remark that triggered Smith's outburst at the 2022 Oscars ceremony. Rock had joked about Jada Pinkett Smith appearing in a sequel to the 1997 movie "G.I. Jane" to poke fun at her shaved head.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Pinkett Smith has spoken about living with alopecia, a condition most associated with hair loss. Her husband, sitting beside her, took offense at the joke, walked onto the stage, and slapped Rock. Under the Academy's recent post, some fans revisited that moment in the comments.
 "That face you make before dropping a G.I. Jane joke," one person wrote about Rock's expression, earning hundreds of likes.
 Another joked, "Still no G.I. JANE 2??" while yet another simply wrote, "Flashbacks."
 Chris Rock Previously Revealed His One Condition For Returning To The Oscars
 MEGA
 In a September interview earlier this year, Rock addressed the possibility of attending the Oscars again. Speaking to Variety , the comedian explained that he would only consider returning to the ceremony as a nominee.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "The only way I'll go back is if I'm nominated, and I'm not getting nominated," Rock said.
 Rock also expressed doubts about hosting the Oscars again, despite previously taking on the role in 2005 and 2016. He acknowledged the talent of more recent hosts, including Conan O'Brien, and suggested his time in that role might have passed.
 As The Blast previously reported , Rock also discussed the slap while promoting "Misty Green." He said he wished the slap had never happened, but did not consider his experience particularly important compared to the problems others face.
 Will Smith's Academy Ban Remains In Place As Chris Rock Insists He Has 'Moved On'
 Lumeimages / MEGA
 Smith faced serious consequences for slapping Rock at the 2022 ceremony. He resigned from the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences and was then hit with a ten-year ban from attending its events, including the Oscars.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The ban began on April 8, 2022, and will remain in effect until 2032. Smith has since apologized to Rock, acknowledging that his behavior was unacceptable.
 Rock, meanwhile, seems determined to leave the controversy in the past. During an October interview with The New York Times, he addressed the incident without expressing any desire to look back on the dispute with Smith.
 "That was so long ago. I wish everyone well. I've moved on with my life," the comedian said.
